content_voiceover: This is the continuation of the ICC classification algorithm, picking up where the previous slide left off, after blasts have been confirmed as below the excess blasts threshold, meaning under 5 to 9 percent marrow or under 2 to 9 percent blood. The next check is for a 5 q deletion. If a 5 q deletion is present, the algorithm then asks whether minus 7 or 7 q deletion is also present. If minus 7 or 7 q deletion is absent, the diagnosis is MDS with del 5 q. If a 5 q deletion is not present at all, the algorithm moves to S F 3 B 1 mutation status with variant allele frequency at least 10 percent. If S F 3 B 1 is mutated, it checks for minus 7, 7 q deletion, abnormality of 3 q 26.2, or complex karyotype. If none of those are present, the diagnosis is MDS with mutated S F 3 B 1. If S F 3 B 1 is not mutated, the algorithm checks R U N X 1 mutation status, and if R U N X 1 is also absent, the pathway loops back toward MDS with mutated S F 3 B 1 by exclusion in this diagram's dashed arrows. Several dashed arrows converge on MDS N O S without dysplasia whenever high risk cytogenetics like minus 7, 7 q deletion, abnormality of 3 q 26.2, complex karyotype, or R U N X 1 mutation are present alongside no dysplasia. Finally, the rightmost branch asks about dysplasia directly. If dysplasia is absent, the case again falls into MDS N O S without dysplasia, and if dysplasia is present, the case is further split into MDS N O S with single lineage dysplasia or MDS N O S with multilineage dysplasia depending on how many lineages are affected.
keypoints: 5 q deletion without minus 7 or 7 q deletion equals MDS with del 5 q
S F 3 B 1 mutation without high risk cytogenetics equals MDS with mutated S F 3 B 1
Minus 7, 7 q deletion, 3 q 26.2 abnormality, complex karyotype, or R U N X 1 route toward MDS N O S without dysplasia
Presence of dysplasia splits MDS N O S into single lineage or multilineage subtypes
This algorithm is the direct continuation of the excess blasts branch from the prior slide
keypoint_voiceover: This slide completes the lower blast count arm of the ICC algorithm. Clean 5 q deletion or clean S F 3 B 1 mutation, without high risk cytogenetic partners, gives you the named molecular subtypes. High risk cytogenetics such as monosomy 7, complex karyotype, or R U N X 1 mutation redirect the case toward MDS N O S without dysplasia, while the presence and extent of dysplasia further separates the remaining N O S cases.
